title: Halting bound for the validity tester
statement: Let $x$, $r$, and $p$ be Boolean words and suppose $x=p\,r$. There is a time $t\le |r|+1$ such that, starting in the block state at position $|p|$ with empty output, the validity tester has halted after $t$ steps and its output is the single bit indicating whether the aligned pair parser successfully decodes $r$.
replaced:
For any split $x = p s$ of the input, there is a time $t \le \abs{s}+1$ such
that after $t$ steps from the block state at position $\abs{p}$ with empty
output, the validity tester has halted and its output is the single bit
recording whether $s$ is a valid self-delimiting pair code.
